workflow_phases.title: Deconstruct Problem & Surface Assumptions
activities: Read the problem statement aloud and clarify ambiguities
Map key stakeholders and who hurts most from the problem
Document baseline assumptions and scope boundaries
workflow_phases.outcome: Clear one-sentence problem statement and agreed assumption log

workflow_phases.title: Profile Personas & Quick Validation
activities: Select one primary persona to anchor the live demo
Draft 5 test inputs including at least 1 edge case
Define concrete acceptance criteria for core user interactions
workflow_phases.outcome: Target persona locked with 5 realistic demo test inputs

workflow_phases.title: Compare Approaches & Select Must-Haves
activities: Weigh 2 to 3 architectural approaches and their trade-offs
Select exactly 3 must-have features for the MVP
workflow_phases.outcome: MVP scope locked to 3 must-haves with trade-offs understood

workflow_phases.title: Implement MVP Core & Connect Demo Flow
activities: Build data storage and API endpoints for must-haves
Implement core business logic or AI brain components
Build screens and connect end-to-end demo flow
workflow_phases.outcome: Working end-to-end flow executing the demo path without crashing

workflow_phases.title: Test Inputs, Bugfix & Check Limits
activities: Run the 5 test inputs through the full application
Fix blocking crashes and polish user feedback messages
Catalog honest system limits and edge case boundaries
workflow_phases.outcome: Verified test input results and documented honest limits

workflow_phases.title: Structure Jury Deck & Rehearse Pitch
activities: Complete the 6-slide jury outline with proof points
Prepare concise answers for likely jury technical questions
workflow_phases.outcome: Rehearsed 3-minute pitch and polished live demo readiness

task_templates.title: Read the problem aloud and write the one-sentence problem
Pick one persona and ask 2 real people how they handle this today
Write 5 test inputs including 1 edge case
Choose 2 to 3 must-have features from the brief
Build the data storage and API for the must-haves
Build the core logic or AI for the must-haves
Build the screens for the demo path
Connect all parts and run one full path
Run the test inputs and fix critical issues only
Write the 6-slide outline and rehearse the demo twice

checkpoints.check: Problem and persona validated with one-sentence clarity
checkpoints.how: Confirm the team agrees on the one persona and their single biggest daily friction point.
Verify that all 3 must-haves are assigned to owners and nice-to-haves are postponed.
Execute one round-trip from frontend UI input to backend response without crashing.

checkpoints.check: Live demo rehearsed twice with known limits ready
checkpoints.how: Time a 3-minute run-through following the demo script and confirm honest limits slide.

jury_slides.title: Problem
jury_slides.proof: Quote real user friction and contrast with today's manual workarounds.

jury_slides.title: Who it hurts
jury_slides.proof: Persona profile with validated quotes and daily impact metrics.

jury_slides.title: Our approach
jury_slides.proof: Architecture diagram showing why this approach balances speed and reliability.

jury_slides.title: Live demo
jury_slides.proof: Unbroken 90-second live walkthrough of the core must-have path.

jury_slides.title: Does it work
jury_slides.proof: Execution logs of test inputs and acceptance criteria pass rate.

jury_slides.title: Limits and next steps
jury_slides.proof: Transparent list of current assumptions, edge case limits, and roadmap.

demo_tips: Open all required browser tabs, terminal windows, and test inputs before the judges arrive.
Show the live working product first within 60 seconds; do not spend half your time on background slides.
Use realistic pre-prepared demo inputs rather than typing slowly or testing random inputs live.
If an error occurs, state calmly what was expected, explain the limit honestly, and continue the flow.

Problem clarity.question: Who is your primary user and how exactly did you validate this pain point?
Problem clarity.why_asked: Jury wants to ensure you built for real human needs rather than an abstract idea.
Problem clarity.answer_hint: Name your specific persona, cite your interview or survey findings, and quantify how often this pain occurs.

Problem clarity.question: Why can't users solve this with existing tools like WhatsApp or Excel today?
Problem clarity.why_asked: Tests whether you understand current alternatives and genuine workflow bottlenecks.
Problem clarity.answer_hint: Highlight what makes manual tools fail at scale, such as lack of automation, data loss, or delay.

Problem clarity.question: What single metric defines success for this project in production?
Problem clarity.why_asked: Measures whether your solution outcome is measurable and tangible.
Problem clarity.answer_hint: Give a specific number, such as 30% reduction in turnaround time or 90% completion rate.

Works end to end.question: Can we see the end-to-end flow run from raw input to final output live?
Works end to end.why_asked: Distinguishes working prototypes from mocked UI screenshots.
Works end to end.answer_hint: Walk through your demo path in order: input submission, backend processing, and final visible result.

Works end to end.question: Which components in this flow are fully dynamic and which are simulated?
Works end to end.why_asked: Evaluates honesty about the boundary between prototype and production.
Works end to end.answer_hint: Be direct: state which APIs and data stores are live, and acknowledge any static mock data.

Works end to end.question: What happens if a user submits invalid or empty data at step one?
Works end to end.why_asked: Tests basic defensive programming and error handling sanity.
Works end to end.answer_hint: Show your form validation message and confirm the system fails safely with a readable error.

Scope realism.question: Why did you prioritize these specific must-have features over the rest?
Scope realism.why_asked: Checks trade-off judgment and ability to scope ruthlessly under time constraints.
Scope realism.answer_hint: Explain how these core features deliver the minimum believable value for your target persona.

Scope realism.question: What features did you intentionally cut to ensure a stable demo?
Scope realism.why_asked: Rewords scope discipline as a strength rather than a failure.
Scope realism.answer_hint: List your postponed nice-to-haves and show how cutting them kept your demo path robust.

Scope realism.question: How realistic is completing the remaining backlog given your team size and timeline?
Scope realism.why_asked: Assesses project management awareness and execution velocity.
Scope realism.answer_hint: Reference your effort budget points and explain your next scheduled development sprint.

Innovation and practicality.question: What is genuinely innovative about your approach compared to standard solutions?
Innovation and practicality.why_asked: Probes for creative problem-solving beyond standard CRUD tutorials.
Innovation and practicality.answer_hint: Point to your specific rule automation, lightweight architecture, or novel user touchpoint.

Innovation and practicality.question: How does this solution handle practical constraints like offline access or low budget?
Innovation and practicality.why_asked: Tests real-world engineering viability and operational cost awareness.
Innovation and practicality.answer_hint: Discuss your zero-cost stack choices, low compute overhead, or offline-friendly design.

Innovation and practicality.question: What is the biggest operational risk if this were deployed tomorrow?
Innovation and practicality.why_asked: Checks whether you recognize real deployment hurdles like user compliance or data quality.
Innovation and practicality.answer_hint: Highlight a real adoption barrier and your proposed mitigation plan.

Can you explain it.question: Can you explain your system architecture and data flow in 60 seconds?
Can you explain it.why_asked: Verifies technical mastery and clear communication under pressure.
Can you explain it.answer_hint: Describe frontend input, API request handling, business logic execution, and database state cleanly.

Can you explain it.question: What was the most challenging technical bug your team solved during the build?
Can you explain it.why_asked: Proves that the team actually wrote and debugged the code.
Can you explain it.answer_hint: Describe the specific bug, how you diagnosed it, and the fix you implemented.

Can you explain it.question: What are the clear boundaries and known limits of this prototype today?
Can you explain it.why_asked: Evaluates intellectual honesty, which judges respect far more than overpromising.
Can you explain it.answer_hint: State 2 clear current limitations candidly and explain what research or work would solve them.

summary_short.action: Expand idea summary to at least 20 words describing the core problem and who suffers.

missing_persona.action: Name your specific persona and key stakeholder explicitly in the project summary.

missing_metric.action: Add a concrete number or percentage goal to your summary (e.g. reduce wait by 30%).

missing_validation.action: Add a sentence explaining how you spoke to or interviewed real users about this issue.

missing_must_haves.action: Connect at least one additional must-have feature into your live running flow.

missing_demo_script.action: Write out a step-by-step 4-line demo script showing exactly what to click and enter.

no_features.action: List the core features built so the jury can assess your working scope.

overscoped.action: Trim non-essential feature promises and focus exclusively on your 3 must-haves.

time_crunch.action: With under 15 minutes left, freeze new code and polish only the working path.

missing_innovative.action: Highlight your innovative feature and explain the specific advantage it provides.

missing_constraints.action: Explain in your summary how your solution respects cost, time, or privacy constraints.

missing_limits.action: List at least two honest technical limits to demonstrate mature engineering judgment.

missing_baseline.action: Contrast your tool against what users do today (e.g. manual spreadsheets or paper).

empty_demo_script.action: Document your live demo walk-through steps so any team member can present it.

short_demo_script.action: Expand your demo script into 4 clear steps: input, processing, output, and result.

missing_limits.action: Identify at least one clear operational boundary to show honest self-awareness.

summary_length.action: Refine the idea summary to be between 20 and 120 words for quick jury reading.
